Copper & landline (POTS) retirement tracker · data as of · statuses re-checked

Dates come from public FCC and carrier filings and are the earliest dates the carrier says it may act. They are not scheduled disconnection dates. Carriers notify affected customers by letter, and some send a second letter with the specific date. Pending filings can change or be denied. A listing means a filing covers part of this area, not that every line in the ZIP is affected. Confirm with your carrier.

How to read a listing

Date passed the carrier may now act; customers are notified by letter
Copper retirement date passed
Within 6 mo6–12 moPending FCC approvalOn hold: FCC review
  • Landline service ending: the phone company has FCC approval, or has asked for it, to stop offering traditional phone service. The date is the earliest it may disconnect, not a scheduled shutoff. Customers get a letter from the carrier, and Verizon and Frontier send a second letter with the actual date.
  • Copper being retired: the carrier is removing copper wire and moving service to fiber or wireless. Phone service may continue on the new network, but alarm panels, elevator phones and fax lines often need testing or new equipment to work on it.
  • Match: Exact: the ZIP appears in the carrier's own address list. Community: a central office named in the filing serves this town. Most filings cover only part of a central office's area, so not every address in the ZIP is affected.

What this covers

Filings from AT&T, Verizon and Frontier (a Verizon company since Jan 20, 2026), Lumen/CenturyLink, Windstream, Consolidated, altafiber and Hawaiian Telcom with dates in the filing from through .

Sources are FCC Section 214 public notices, carrier copper-retirement notices under 47 CFR 51.333, and copies of carrier filings at state utility commissions. Each listing links to its source.

Some filings name only states, not wire centers. Those appear as state notices in the copper-colored boxes.

AT&T "Wireless First" office closings are not listed: AT&T's notices say no working copper lines remain on the retired copper.

FCC rule changes to the copper retirement and discontinuance process (FCC 26-19) take effect Oct 15, 2026. A court challenge is pending in the 9th Circuit (No. 26-3946). Source

Before you rely on it

Carriers file new notices every month. For copper retirement, the FCC does not require carriers to notify end customers directly, so the first sign is often a letter from your carrier. A listing means a filing exists, not that a specific line will be cut on that date. Check for a letter from the carrier for the address, and plan the replacement for fire alarm, elevator, emergency phone and fax lines early.
